candidates.status: equivalent metadata consolidation candidate; coordinate with active HP feature owner before any edit
candidates.finding: Two per-engine sets repeat immutable catalog predicates. They overlap but have different contracts: HP capability ids are the strict HP-grant subset; HP-sensitive ids additionally contain suppression-only definitions, including definitions with no Program. The MatchSkillBindingIndex callback uses the broad set to decide whether current HP belongs in the rebuild stamp. The synchronization guard uses the strict subset to detect raw currently enabled sources.
minimal_change: Compile two ordinal FrozenSet<string> values in the existing per-registry SkillProgramDependencies, using its already materialized ContentSkillDefinition[] definitions. Suggested exposed contracts: IReadOnlySet<string> HpSensitiveSkillIds and HpConditionalCapabilitySkillIds.

The strict set uses exactly skill.Program?.HpSkillGrants.Count > 0. The broad set uses exactly skill.SuppressionRule is not null OR the strict predicate. Preserve StringComparer.Ordinal. Iterate definitions rather than programs so a suppression-only skill with no Program is included.

GameEngine's MatchSkillBindingIndex callback reads player.SkillGrants.HasEnabledSkill(contentRegistry.ProgramDependencies.HpSensitiveSkillIds). Remove only the constructor-local HashSet creation and captured set, not the callback or CurrentHp stamp.

SynchronizeHpConditionalSkillGrants reads the registry's strict set for the existing empty-catalog and raw-membership guards. Remove only the engine readonly field and constructor assignment; retain the dynamic retained-instance count gate and all synchronization/qualification behavior.
do_not_conflate: Do not replace both sets with the broad union: suppression-only skills must not count as HP-grant capability sources.
Do not replace both sets with the strict subset: suppression-only owned skills must still invalidate the current binding shard when HP changes.

Do not derive the catalog sets from only match-start generals, currently effective binding shards, trigger operations or active programs. A legal HP-grant capability can have no triggers/operations and can be granted after construction.

Preserve HasEnabledSkill's raw enabled-grant membership. Using an already qualified shard instead risks excluding a newly introduced source or retained cleanup work and can couple synchronization to its own qualification/cache path.
focused_validation_additions: Extend the existing whole-catalog dependency check with exact set equivalence against the original source predicates for normal/classic/custom registries, ordinal identities, frozen collection behavior and separate-registry isolation.

Include an unowned program with only HP-grant capability and no trigger/activation operations, an unowned suppression-only definition with no Program, and plain negatives. Assert strict subset and broad union independently.

Retain the existing HP-sensitive suppression shard invalidation and ordinary-HP-change shard reuse assertions. Retain dynamic grant introduction, source disable/removal, retained-instance identity, threshold exits/reentry, privacy and paid continuation tests.
